page: Microsoft Azure FX24mds_v2 is a high-frequency, memory-intensive virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by a dedicated 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, providing 24 vCPUs across 12 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration features a substantial 260 MB L3 cache alongside hardware support for Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 vector instructions. System resources include 504.0 GB of RAM—yielding 21.0 GB per vCPU—and a bundled 1417 GB local NVMe SSD. It contains no onboard GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional single-thread performance, driven by the sustained 4.2 GHz clock speed and large cache hierarchy. The instance achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core execution (2367.0) along with top-tier image and text processing scores. Data decompression and compression routines, including single-threaded gzip (34.92 GB/sec) and bzip3 (14.34 GB/sec), perform in the top quartile. CPU-based inference workloads on smaller language models (135M) reach top-tier throughput at 408.05 tokens per second. In contrast, multi-core throughput metrics, such as PassMark CPU score (41703.39) and stress-ng multi-core (26660.04), sit within the median performance bracket.

By pairing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio with elevated clock frequencies, the FX24mds_v2 delivers strong efficiency for workloads constrained by per-core software licensing and memory footprints. The onboard 1417 GB NVMe SSD provides low-latency temporary scratch space without additional storage provisioning costs. The primary architectural tradeoff is lower total multithreaded capacity compared to platforms with higher vCPU densities. This instance profile is well suited for in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), financial modeling, batch analytics, and data pipeline processing.
